en.dek: Military leaders push back elections originally scheduled for December 6 by two years, extending the transition period.
body: Military leaders in Guinea-Bissau announced a delay to presidential and legislative elections until 2028.
The decision follows the military's seizure of power on 26 November 2025.
Africanews reported the military rulers pushed back elections by two years, extending the transition period.
Al Jazeera reported military leaders stated the presidential and legislative poll scheduled for December 6 will now take place in November 2028.
BBC and AllAfrica confirmed the delay was announced after the military's seizure of power on 26 November 2025.
The delay extends the transition period beyond the originally scheduled December 6 vote.
Military leaders justified the postponement by citing the need to ensure a credible electoral process.
Reports indicate the military justified the move as necessary to allow sufficient time for voter registration and campaign preparations.
